To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a mathematical model of tumor evolution can be used to determine tumor volume regression patterns and radio-sensitivity, and that the latter can be related with the MRI-based indicators TOLD and ΔR2*, which are related to oxygenation.

(1) a simple mathematical model can be used to describe tumor response to radiation therapy; (2) this model can identify different radio-sensitivity patterns in tumors; (3) radio-sensitivity can be correlated with MRI-based oxygenation indicators.
the mathematical model was able to classify the tumors according to their radio-sensitivity and that the radio-sensitivity was correlated with the variation of ΔR2* after oxygen breathing challenge.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of a possible correlation between MRI-based indicators of tumor oxygenation and the radio-sensitivity.
a mathematical model of tumor growth and response to radiation, and with the use of this model to correlate the MRI-based indicators with radio-sensitivity.
the development and validation of mathematical models to describe tumor response to radiotherapy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model was not able to provide a satisfactory description of the experimental data, and that no significant correlation was found with the oxygenation parameters.
the model can identify different tumor regression patterns and that ΔR2* can be a predictor of the radio-sensitivity.
MRI can be useful for the assessment of the tumor response to radiation therapy, but further investigations are needed to better understand its role.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radio-sensitivity is a function of the tumor microenvironment, which can be investigated by means of non-invasive techniques, such as MRI.
the tumor oxygenation status can be evaluated by means of a single dose of irradiation, which can be administered to the tumor prior to the treatment.
the MRI-based indices of oxygenation are not good indicators of radio-sensitivity, but they can be used as indicators of tumor response to oxygen breathing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the mathematical modeling approach is a promising tool to identify and characterize tumor subpopulations with different radio-sensitivity.
MRI may be used to predict radio-sensitivity, and therefore to optimize radiation therapy.

, although a simple mathematical model can provide a reasonable approximation of the tumor volume evolution, its fitting performance is not sufficient to be used for a reliable prediction of the tumor volume at any given time point.
